what: Dev-only test of the zero-candidate fallback (drishyam.agent JobConfig.fallback_l2: when the overview proposes no candidate, one look at L2 whose window spans the whole photo before the job ends, cause fallback-l2) for the live v1 segmenter, at the 30 % pixel cap. Never a held-out set. Pre-registration stub: the rule, the variants, the splits, the commands and the choices below were committed before any run of this test was made or read; the rows, the counts, the decision and the verdict are added after, and these fields are not changed then.
motivation: The team's wall photo IMG_2332 (public/samples/real_01.jpg, no ground truth): its saliency peaks at about 0.22 against the 0.5 threshold, so the overview proposes no candidate, no look runs and the photo is reported not assessed, although a hairline crack is visible by eye. In the 2026-10-21 re-grade a read-only probe (judge Gary Bradski) ran the v1 net on a whole-photo L3 view (the survey's scale) and saw 0 crack pixels, and on a whole-photo L2 view about 5,080 (private-assets/regrade-2026-10-21-released.json, reviews[Bradski], merged.top_changes item 5). real_01 is the motivation only, never evidence: it has no ground truth, and no run of this test reads it.
segmenter: onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx (v1, the released weights c49416c10087...; fp16 file beside it, unused with the governor's overrides off), under its own profile onnx:drishyam_dacl10k.onnx (min_view 0.3, absorb off), resolved by name and weights in every job
costs: fixed: the job_ops p50 ms per call of results/local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime/micro.json, the table v1's dev comparison (results/dev/model_choice_dev.json) and its held-out runs (results/heldout_models.json) were charged; governor overrides off (evals.harness.run_drishyam), caps and KILL on. Every look, the fallback's included, is charged its warp, quality and segment:accurate p50, timed at a 512-px gaze: the fallback's gaze is larger (the long side / 4 px), so its warp and quality are undercharged by a few ms; the net's input is 512 x 512 whatever the gaze (the ONNX letterboxes it), so its segment cost is the timed one.

variants.cur: fallback_l2 False: v1 as released (v1.1.0, main ae16bd8), the reference, listed first in every run

choices: Stated before the run. Scope: fallback_l2 is a JobConfig field, not a profile value, so it applies to every profile alike (classical-v1, v1, v2a, v2b, v2c): the trigger (an overview with no candidate) does not depend on the segmenter, and the look runs the profile's own accurate net under the profile's own rules. The rule below is measured on v1 only, the live engine. If it is adopted the default becomes True for every profile; the classical engine's and v2a-v2c's published numbers, which ran before it, stay those of the flag off and are not re-run (said wherever they are reported beside it).

The look: level 2 under every profile (its window spans the whole photo, more than any profile's min_view share), a gaze of max(512, ceil(long side / 4)) px centred on the photo (on a photo of 2048 px or more, the L2 image itself), with the accurate net; pixels charged gaze x gaze, 8.3 % of a 4:3 photo of 2048 px or more (more on a smaller one: on 1024 x 768, 33 %, above the 30 % cap). The governor checks KILL and the caps before it as before any look: a cap it would exceed halts the job (cap-hit) with no look, and the photo stays not assessed.

Follow-ups: the look goes through the normal rules, so a mask it is unsure of, or a new mask, is escalated or verified one level finer where the profile allows it (under v1's min_view 0.3: L1 on photos of 2048 px to about 3400 px; none on CODEBRIM's 3648-px and larger photos, where L2 is v1's finest level). Those looks are part of fb and count in its recall, boxes and ms.

The work order: the photo keeps its not-assessed entry (no candidate region was proposed, check-by-eye) whatever the look drafts, so it is never ready; what the look and its follow-ups draft is reported like any look's findings, critical ones held for the human gate as before. coverage_looked does not count the fallback look (a whole-photo look is no closer than the survey). A job killed after the fallback look resumes into the same job (the replay accepts that look's gaze).

Scoring: evals.harness's matching (a box finds a ground-truth box of its class when it contains its centre or overlaps it at IoU >= 0.3) over per-component boxes (preds), as every dev row; on the clean split every box is a false alarm.
rule: Stated before any run of this test. Reference: cur, listed first, so fb is paired with it on the same photos and the same cost table (evals.dev_sweep's vs_ref fields: paired 95 % bootstrap CIs over images, 1000 resamples, seed 0). fallback_l2 is adopted (becomes the default) only if, for v1 at the 30 % pixel cap, ALL of: (1) recall does not drop on synth_dev (60 photos, seed 4242): fb's recall ratio to cur (vs_ref) is >= 1 AND its paired CI (vs_ref_ci) includes 1 or lies above it (upper bound >= 1); (2) the same on CODEBRIM dev100 (evals/codebrim_dev100.txt); (3) clean false alarms do not rise on synth_clean_dev (30 photos, seed 4243): the paired CI of fb's boxes-per-photo difference to cur (boxes_diff_vs_ref_ci) includes 0 or lies below it (lower bound <= 0), AND the paired CI of its difference in the share of photos with any box (images_with_any_vs_ref_ci) includes 0 or lies below it. Otherwise it is not adopted: the code stays behind fallback_l2, default off. The fallback acts only on photos with no candidate, so on any other photo fb equals cur; a split with no such photo passes its clause trivially (ratio 1, CI [1, 1]; difference 0, CI [0, 0]), and the count of such photos per split is reported beside the verdict so that a pass resting on few or no photos is visible. Decided on these dev splits only; real_01 is never read by it. If adopted, v1 with the fallback is scored once on the held-out sets (CODEBRIM eval200, synth200, synth_clean) as v1's third read, with the recipe of its earlier held-out runs, and published beside v1's numbers, never over them; nothing is changed after that read.
reported_not_in_rule: per split: the photos the fallback acted on (fb jobs with a fallback-l2 look; checked equal to the cur jobs with no look, which at the 30 % cap are exactly the photos with no candidate), the looks it added and at which levels and causes, modelled ms per job for cur and fb and their paired ratio CI, the extra modelled ms per photo acted on, recall, IoU-only recall, chance recall and boxes per photo on the recall splits, critical boxes per photo (the human gate's load), what was drafted on the photos acted on, and whether cur reproduces v1's rows in results/dev/model_choice_dev.json (same photos, same table).

splits.clean: data/synth_clean_dev, 30 photos with no damage, seed 4243
splits.real: CODEBRIM dev100: evals/codebrim_dev100.txt in data/codebrim (none in eval200)
splits.check: each split's dataset sha256 (ground truth and images) must equal results/dev/model_choice_dev.json's datasets

commands: bash runs/fallback/sweep.sh, which for split in synth_dev clean real runs: DRISHYAM_ONNX=models/drishyam_dacl10k.onnx DRISHYAM_ONNX_FP16=models/drishyam_dacl10k.fp16.onnx PYTHONPATH=<the worktree> .venv/bin/python -m evals.dev_sweep <split> 0.3 "cur=fallback_l2:False;fb=fallback_l2:True" --workers 6 --micro-arm local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime --codebrim data/codebrim --out runs/fallback/<split>.json --dump runs/fallback/<split>.dump.json.gz, and logs the code commit, the tracked changes and the load at the start and end of each split in runs/fallback/log.txt
then the rows, counts and verdict are read from runs/fallback/<split>.json and the dumps into this file by the rule above, unchanged
if_adopted_held_out: Each held-out set once, v1 with fallback_l2 on (the new default), as v1's earlier held-out runs (runs/heldout/run_model.sh dacl10k local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime): the dacl10k-vs-CODEBRIM leakage check (evals.leakage) first; then python -m evals.harness --cost-model fixed --micro-arm local-macos-x86-dacl10k-retime --workers 6 with DRISHYAM_ONNX set, on data/codebrim (--n 200: eval200.txt), data/synth200 (--n 200, seed 7) and data/synth_clean (--n 51 --seed 11 --chaos 0,0,0), into runs/model-eval/onnx-fb-<set>; every job's switches must say fallback_l2 True; then python -m evals.heldout adds them to results/heldout_models.json as a new model "v1+fallback" beside v1 (whose runs are not repeated), with prior_exposure saying how often v1 was read on these sets before (CODEBRIM eval200 and synth200 twice, synth_clean once: evals.heldout.PRIOR and its published runs) and that this configuration was chosen on dev after those reads. Nothing is written to public/.
decision: Adopted by the rule as stated (every clause holds): fallback_l2 becomes the default, for every profile. The pass rests on 1 of 190 dev photos: no photo of synth_dev or of the clean dev split has zero candidates under v1 (0 of 60, 0 of 30), so on them fb equals cur photo for photo and their clauses pass trivially (recall x1.00, CI 1.00-1.00; clean differences 0, CIs [0, 0]); in particular no clean photo exercised the false-alarm clause. On CODEBRIM dev100 the fallback acted on 1 photo of 100 (2048x1536): its fallback look at L2 and a verify look at L1 drafted 2 crack boxes and found 1 of its 1 ground-truth box, which cur missed (0): recall x1.0025 (CI 1.00-1.0093), boxes per photo 39.12 to 39.14, no critical box added. Modelled cost: +1183.3 ms on that photo (two looks of about 592 ms on the 2048x1536 row of the table), +11.8 ms per job over dev100 (x1.0035, CI 1.00-1.0135). That is the rule's outcome; it does not show the fallback helps in general, only that on these dev splits it cost no recall and added no false alarm, and it acted on almost nothing.
notes: On every photo the fallback did not act on, fb's trace, boxes and modelled seconds equal cur's (asserted), so every difference comes from the photos counted in acted_on.

cur reproduces v1's dev rows in results/dev/model_choice_dev.json photo for photo (found, IoU-only found, ground truth, boxes and modelled ms; the chance columns are seeded by the row's name): cur_reproduces_v1_in_model_choice_dev.
acted_on.real.indices index the split's photo order (evals/codebrim_dev100.txt as harness.load_records reads it); no CODEBRIM photo or name is stored here.
the costs are a fixed table on a virtual clock, so the machine load in run.log (up to about 56) changes no row.

run.order_checked: the rule commit's time is before the run log's and every split log's creation (asserted)
